questions.q: How does a pipeline-health alert differ from Lesson 37's Activator data alerts?
options: Activator can't be used for any kind of alerting at all
Pipeline-health alerts only apply to batch pipelines, never streaming ones
They are exactly the same mechanism with a different name
It watches the pipeline itself failing — like a notebook exception or an Eventstream disconnecting — rather than watching data values
questions.explain: Both matter, but they're triggered by completely different conditions and usually need different people to see them.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which situation deserves an immediate page?
options: A KQL query running 200ms slower than its rolling average
A single event failing a data quality check that's already being routed elsewhere
None of these situations deserve any kind of alert
An Eventstream disconnecting from its source, since data has stopped flowing entirely
questions.explain: A disconnected Eventstream means a human needs to act right now; the other situations can be logged and reviewed later.

options: A technical limit on how many alerts a system can send per day
The delay between an alert firing and a human seeing it
A feature that automatically silences all alerts after a set time
The problem where too many low-value alerts cause people to start ignoring pages, including the one time it's a real, serious problem
questions.explain: This is the single most common reason alerting systems fail in practice.

questions.q: Why is "add more alerts" the wrong fix for alert fatigue?
options: More alerts make it easier for people to ignore all of them equally
The real fix is being deliberate about which conditions genuinely warrant interrupting a person's day, not increasing alert volume
Alert fatigue isn't actually caused by alert volume at all
Adding more alerts always solves the underlying problem completely
questions.explain: More noise makes the fatigue problem worse, not better — the fix is precision, not volume.

options: They automatically resolve every alert without human involvement
They eliminate the need for any human on-call rotation
They only apply to data alerts, never pipeline-health alerts
They match the response urgency to the actual stakes, so nobody gets woken up at 2am for a low-severity issue and nothing critical waits until morning
questions.explain: Lesson 68 (On-Call for Data Engineers) picks this exact structure back up when covering who receives each tier.
